persona.note: quit my job last week to go all in on our brand. no money yet but honestly ive never felt more alive. i want to stay like this and not lose this fire when it gets hard

understanding.emotion: alive and afraid of losing it
understanding.bridge: What you are living with is what the texts call starting what is yours to build, and that is where this week begins.
understanding.week_thesis: The fire you feel now is not the problem. The grip on the result before it arrives is what will put it out, and this week you learn to let go.

week_beats.hook: You recognise the fire and the fear of losing it, named without judgement.
week_beats.diagnose: You see that the resolve is tested not by the money but by the mind reaching for the result before it arrives.
week_beats.steady: You hold that no honest effort on the right path is ever wasted, and the work itself is the reward.
week_beats.story: A young builder who bet everything on a dream and kept their resolve through the first empty month shows you how.

understanding.core_struggle: Has quit their job to build a brand, feels more alive than ever, and is determined not to lose this fire when the money runs out.
understanding.mirror: You quit your job, and for the first time in a long time you feel like you are actually alive.
understanding.insight: You are not losing the fire. You are about to discover whether the fire is in the doing or in the result. The one you choose is the one that lasts.

queries.hook: A fire lit by seeing what others achieved; the resolve to rise, gather your strength and take on what is yours to do.
queries.diagnose: Resolve fades when the mind runs ahead to the prize; it holds when the work itself is the reward.
queries.steady: No honest effort on the right path is ever wasted; even a little of it protects you and carries you forward.
queries.act: Rise and act; do your work fully and well each day, let the result go, and keep at it when no one is watching.
queries.story: A young builder who bet everything on a dream, faced the first empty month, and kept their resolve by loving the work itself.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna on duties by nature and finding fulfilment in your own work.
verse.sanskrit: श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात् । स्वभावनियतं कर्म कुर्वन्नाप्नोति किल्बिषम् ॥
verse.line: Better your own path, imperfectly walked, than someone else's done perfectly.
verse.translation: Better is one's own duty, though imperfect, than the duty of another well performed. Doing the work born of one's own nature, one incurs no wrong.
verse.why: Do the work that fits you, flaws and all, as an offering.
verse.misuse: Not 'stick to the role you were born into'. It's about honest fit with your own nature, not caste or family script.

prasang.title: Duties by nature, and their fruit
prasang.summary: After listing duties by varna, Krishna says one reaches perfection through one's own work done as worship, and that one's own path, though imperfect, beats another's, since every undertaking has flaws.
prasang.lesson: Do the work that fits you, flaws and all, as an offering.

verse.meaning: Krishna is speaking to Arjuna on the battlefield. The armies are lined up and about to clash. Arjuna is frozen, unsure of his place. Krishna tells him to look at his own nature. He says that doing the work that fits your own nature, even if it is flawed, is better than doing someone else's work perfectly. The work born of your own nature brings no fault. The idea is to offer your own imperfect path as a form of worship.
verse.for_you: You have left your old life behind and the work feels like it belongs to you now. That fire is real. The fear comes from wondering if this feeling will last. But the work itself, the act of building, is what keeps the flame alive.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on working in the world without being stained by it.
verse.sanskrit: युक्तः कर्मफलं त्यक्त्वा शान्तिमाप्नोति नैष्ठिकीम् । अयुक्तः कामकारेण फले सक्तो निबध्यते ॥
verse.line: Let go of the payoff and you find lasting peace. Chase it and it chains you.
verse.translation: The disciplined person, giving up the fruit of action, attains lasting peace. The undisciplined, attached to the fruit and driven by desire, is bound.
verse.why: Be in the mess without letting it soak in.
verse.misuse: Letting go of the payoff isn't refusing fair pay or recognition; it's not being chained to it.

matched.label: I'm anxious about how things will turn out

prasang.title: Marks of the knower and the doer
prasang.summary: The disciplined person acts without attachment, like a lotus leaf untouched by water, and finds peace by letting go of the fruit.
prasang.lesson: Be in the mess without letting it soak in.

verse.meaning: Krishna is telling Arjuna how to move through the world without getting stained by it. He says the disciplined person gives up the fruit of their action and finds lasting peace. The undisciplined person, driven by desire and attached to the result, gets bound. The idea is to be in the mess without letting it soak in.
verse.for_you: The fire you feel right now is the doing, not the money. When the hard month comes, let the work itself be the reward. Stay in the mess without letting it soak in, and trust the path you chose.

verse.speaker: Bhartrihari
verse.sanskrit: निन्दन्तु नीतिनिपुणा यदि वा स्तुवन्तु लक्ष्मीः समाविशतु गच्छतु वा यथेष्टम् । अद्यैव वा मरणमस्तु युगान्तरे वा न्याय्यात्पथः प्रविचलन्ति पदं न धीराः ॥
verse.line: Let them praise or blame, let money come or go: the steady don't step off the right path.
verse.translation: Let the worldly-wise blame or praise; let fortune come or go as she pleases; let death come today or ages hence: the steadfast do not move a step from the path of what is right.
verse.why: Setbacks rarely last for those who keep going on the right path.

prasang.title: Nitishatakam: On steadfastness
prasang.summary: Steadfastness: the gods kept churning the ocean past jewels and poison until they found nectar; the steady do not leave the right path whatever people say. A struck ball bounces back and a cut tree grows again.
prasang.lesson: Setbacks rarely last for those who keep going on the right path.

verse.meaning: Bhartrihari speaks to the reader from the section on steadfastness, right after warning that chasing results chains you. He says the worldly-wise will blame or praise, fortune will come or go, and death will come today or ages hence. The steady do not move a step from the path of what is right, whether money comes or goes. The point is that setbacks rarely last for those who keep going on the right path, and the work itself is the reward.
verse.for_you: Your brand is the path you chose. The praise and the silence, the money and the empty bank account, they are just weather. The fire you feel is not in the outcome. It is in the next honest step you take today.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on how to act without being chained to results.
verse.sanskrit: नेहाभिक्रमनाशोऽस्ति प्रत्यवायो न विद्यते । स्वल्पमप्यस्य धर्मस्य त्रायते महतो भयात् ॥
verse.line: No sincere effort here is ever wasted. Even a little of it shields you from great fear.
verse.translation: On this path no effort is lost and no harm results. Even a little of this practice protects one from great fear.
verse.why: Do the work fully; let go of owning the result.

prasang.title: The yoga of action
prasang.summary: Krishna teaches the yoga of action: work wholeheartedly, give up clinging to outcomes, stay even in success and failure, and keep a single steady purpose.
prasang.lesson: Do the work fully; let go of owning the result.

verse.meaning: Arjuna sits in the chariot, the two armies waiting. Krishna tells him to fight, but not for victory or defeat, only for the action itself. On this path no effort is lost and no harm results. Even a little of this practice protects one from great fear. The work itself is the shelter. It asks you to do what is yours to do, and let the world keep its noise. The result is not your burden to carry.
verse.for_you: You quit your job last week. You have no money yet. This verse says that your effort is already enough. The work of building your brand is the shield you need. Trust the doing, and let the result be what it will.

verse.speaker: Medhavin
verse.setting: A young man named Medhavin urges his father not to keep postponing what truly matters.
verse.sanskrit: श्वः कार्यमद्य कुर्वीत पूर्वाह्णे चापराह्णिकम् / नहि प्रतीक्षते मृत्युः कृतमस्य न वा कृतम्
verse.line: Do tomorrow's work today, and the afternoon's in the morning. Time doesn't wait for you to be ready.
verse.translation: Do tomorrow's work today, and the afternoon's work in the morning. Death does not wait to see whether your work is done or not.
verse.why: Life slips away while we stay busy. Do what matters now.
verse.misuse: About not postponing what matters, not about working nonstop.

prasang.title: Medhavin: the son who woke his father
prasang.summary: A father lays out the conventional path of study, family and ritual. His son Medhavin replies that days and nights fall like arrows and death takes people mid-task, so do tomorrow's work today and live truthfully now.
prasang.lesson: Life slips away while we stay busy. Do what matters now.

verse.meaning: In the Mokshadharma Parva, a young man named Medhavin speaks to his father. He sees the older man laying out a life of study and ritual, but Medhavin tells him to do tomorrow's work today, and the afternoon's in the morning. He says death does not wait to see if your work is done, so time does not wait for you to be ready. The verse asks you to stop waiting for the perfect moment and to act on what matters right now.
verse.for_you: You feel more alive than ever right now. Let that feeling push you to do one small thing for the brand today. Do not wait for the money to arrive to start the work.

verse.speaker: Angada
verse.setting: The monkeys searching for Sita are exhausted and failing; young Angada rallies them.
verse.sanskrit: अवश्यं कुर्वतां तस्य दृश्यते कर्मणः फलम्। परं निर्वेदमागम्य नहि नोन्मीलनं क्षमम्॥
verse.line: Keep working and the results will come. Sink into despair and it is hard to get back up.
verse.translation: Those who keep working surely see the fruit of their work. But once you sink into deep despair, you cannot rise again.
verse.why: Missing a deadline feels final; it rarely is.

prasang.title: The missed deadline
prasang.summary: The southern search party loses time in a magic cave and misses Sugriva's deadline. Angada rallies them once, then despairs, fearing punishment and certain he will be blamed. Hanuman reasons with him to return.
prasang.story_hook: They came out of the cave to find that spring had already come, and their deadline had gone.
prasang.lesson: Missing a deadline feels final; it rarely is.

verse.meaning: The monkeys searching for Sita have lost their way in a magic cave. Sugriva's deadline has passed, and young Angada knows they will be blamed. He tells the exhausted search party to keep moving, because those who keep working will see the fruit. He warns them that once you sink into deep despair, it is hard to rise again. The verse asks you to trust the work itself, not the result you are waiting for.
verse.for_you: Tomorrow's work can wait, but today's step cannot. Before you sleep, write down one small task that moves your brand forward. Do that alone, without checking if it looks like enough. The work itself is the fruit.

story.title: Building the bridge
story.story_hook: The army stood on the shore with no boats, until a quiet monkey said he knew how to build a bridge.
story.summary: Ram waits three days for the ocean to let him pass, then loses patience. The ocean reveals that Nala can build a bridge; Nala admits his skill and the whole army hauls trees and rocks for five days until the bridge reaches Lanka.
story.lesson: Big things get built by many hands, once someone admits they know how.

anchor.speaker: Nala
anchor.setting: The army is stuck at the ocean; Nala reveals he can build a bridge, which he had not mentioned.
anchor.sanskrit: समर्थश्चाप्यहं सेतुं कर्तुं वै वरुणालये। तस्मादद्यैव बध्नन्तु सेतुं वानरपुङ्गवाः॥
anchor.line: I can build this. Let's start today.
anchor.translation: I too am able to build a bridge across the ocean. So let the best of the monkeys start building it this very day.
anchor.why: Big things get built by many hands, once someone admits they know how.

story.hook_title: Ram's army stood on the shore with no boats, until a quiet monkey spoke up
story.teaser: Ram's army stood on the shore with no boats, until a quiet monkey spoke up
story.for_you: Nala did not wait for the ocean to give him permission, and neither should you. Your brand is the bridge, and your hands are already on the first stone. Start the work today without waiting for the result to prove itself.

script: You left your job last week. The money is not there yet, but the fire is real. You are afraid that when the first hard month comes, the feeling will go out.
On the battlefield, the armies are lined up. Arjuna stands between the two sides, frozen. He is unsure of his place. And Krishna replies:
श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात्, स्वभावनियतं कर्म कुर्वन्नाप्नोति किल्बिषम्.
In plain words: Better your own path, imperfectly walked, than someone else's done perfectly.

This is easier said than done, because the fear of failure is loud. But the work itself, the act of building, is what keeps the flame alive. You do not need to wait for the result to feel alive. The fire is in the doing.

For you, today. You have left your old life behind and the work feels like it belongs to you now. That fire is real. The fear comes from wondering if this feeling will last. But the work itself, the act of building, is what keeps the flame alive.
Does the work feel like it belongs to you now?

depth.life: You quit your job last week. You are building your own brand. You feel more alive than ever and you are afraid this feeling will fade when the money runs out. You are asking if what you are doing is discipline or stubbornness. You want to keep the fire burning when the first hard month comes.
depth.points: The fire is in the doing. You are not losing it. You are about to discover whether the fire is in the doing or in the result. The one you choose is the one that lasts. The fear is not that you will fail. The fear is that you will let go of the doing before the result arrives.
depth.practice: Spend ten minutes today building without checking if it is working. Just do the work.
depth.question: What is the work itself asking of you right now?
